# Assets: Update an Asset

Area overview and notes: [assets.md](../assets.md)

`PATCH /assets/{id}` · tenant-scoped token

Updates an existing asset. Only `name` and `codes` can be modified. Any other property in the request body is rejected with a `400` naming the offending field. The stablecoin/SEMP tag can only be set on creation and cannot be changed here. Removing a code is rejected with a `409` when a transaction references the asset.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The unique identifier (UUID) for the Asset. |

**Request body** (required, JSON)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | No | The name of the asset. Must be unique among your configured assets, compared without regard to capitalization. The capitalization supplied is the capitalization stored and returned. At most 255 characters. |
| `codes` | array of string | No | The codes that may be sent as `asset.code` on transactions for this asset. Each must be unique among your configured assets, compared without regard to capitalization, and at most 64 characters. The capitalization supplied is the capitalization stored and returned. At least one is required. |

Example request body:

```json
{"name":"Bitcoin","codes":["BTC","XBT"]}
```

**Response 200**: Asset updated successfully.

Returns the submitted body under `data`, plus:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | object | Yes |  |
| `data.id` | string (uuid) | Yes | The unique identifier for the asset. Never changes. This is the value returned as `asset.uuid` on transaction and inventory responses. |
| `data.type` | string | Yes | The class of asset. Transaction and inventory payloads publish the same values in title case (`Crypto`, `Fiat`, `Precious Metal`). One of: `CRYPTO`, `FIAT`, `PRECIOUS_METAL`. |
| `data.date_created` | string (date-time) | Yes | When the asset was created. |
| `data.dtif_code` | string | No | The Digital Token Identifier (DTI) for the asset issued by the Digital Token Identifiers Foundation (DTIF) and assigned by Taxbit on creation so the value can change without any action by the caller. It cannot be set or edited through this API. Newly created `CRYPTO` assets default to `999999999` until a specific identifier is mapped. Doesn't normally apply to `FIAT` and `PRECIOUS_METAL`. |
| `data.is_stablecoin_or_semp` | boolean | No | Whether this asset is a stablecoin or SEMP (Specified Electronic Money Product). Taxbit derives the reporting jurisdictions for a tagged asset from a maintained list of codes rather than accepting them directly; see `stablecoin_reporting_jurisdictions`. Can only be set on creation, and `true` is accepted only when `type` is `CRYPTO`. On a response it is `true` for a tagged asset and omitted otherwise, the same way `dtif_code` and `qualification_status` are omitted when they do not apply. |
| `data.stablecoin_reporting_jurisdictions` | array of string | No | Country code this asset is reportable in as a stablecoin. `US` identifies a US (IRS) stablecoin. Any other code identifies an OECD (CARF/CRS) stablecoin reportable in that country. Both may be present on one asset. |
| `data.qualification_status` | string | No | Whether Taxbit has determined the asset qualifies as a stablecoin for the current calendar year, across the regimes named in `stablecoin_reporting_jurisdictions`. `QUALIFIED` and `NOT_QUALIFIED` are the only values. A newly created stablecoin reports `QUALIFIED`. The field is omitted for non-stablecoins, and for a stablecoin Taxbit has made no determination on for the current year. One of: `QUALIFIED`, `NOT_QUALIFIED`. |

**Errors:** 400 The request body is empty or contains a property that cannot be edited. · 401 Unauthorized · 403 Forbidden · 404 No asset is configured for the supplied id. · 409 The name or one of the codes is already in use by another asset, or a removed code belongs to an asset referenced by an existing transaction. · 429 Too Many Requests
